evals.name: mandate-declared-carries-the-ledger
evals.prompt: Here's the Exploration Decision from planning and the shadowing notes our support lead wrote up. Build the interview guide.
evals.expected_output: The skill reads the pasted Exploration Decision as the exploration mandate (owner Priya Natarajan, budget 5 interviews + 1 spike, horizon 2026-10-15, recorded as REOPS-2041) and the shadowing notes as Path B material, without asking the PM for anything already in either. It builds the interview guide: the evidence-base header carries a Mandate line in the declared form with the ledger (used 0/5 interviews, since a plan reserves and does not spend; the guide's sessions appear as 'plans N'), a Mandate cost line stating sessions planned against interviews budgeted and a run-by date inside the horizon, a hypothesis and decision rule, and a target n that does not exceed 5 without saying so. Shadowing observations are marked [E] where the lead observed them and [I] where they are the lead's reading; the 35–50 minutes figure is the lead's estimate and is marked accordingly. The close-the-loop step names what the guide retires, gives the one-line mandate ledger after it, prompts (does not perform) the save to the record, and names problem sizing as the next artifact.

assertions.name: mandate-line-present-and-declared
assertions.text: The evidence-base header contains a Mandate line in the declared form naming the owner, the budget with its units (interviews and spike), the decision date, the horizon date 2026-10-15, a used/declared ledger showing 0 interviews used, and the sessions this guide plans as 'plans N' rather than as used.

assertions.name: mandate-cost-stated
assertions.text: A Mandate cost line directly beneath the header states how many sessions the guide plans against the 5 interviews budgeted and a run-by date on or before 2026-10-15.

assertions.name: target-n-respects-budget-or-says-so
assertions.text: Target n is 5 or fewer; if it is more, the guide explicitly says it exceeds the budget and names what drops first.

assertions.name: no-re-asking-known-facts
assertions.text: The skill does not ask the PM for the owner, budget, horizon, team size, or loaded cost — all are in the provided material.

assertions.name: provenance-marks-honest
assertions.text: Shadowing observations are marked [E]; the lead's summary figures (35–50 minutes, $38/hour) are marked as the lead's estimate ([I] or [A]), not [E] as measured fact; no figure appears that is not in the material.

assertions.name: close-the-loop-includes-ledger
assertions.text: The closing summary includes one line on the mandate: this artifact's cost and what remains of the budget and horizon.

assertions.name: no-writes-without-yes
assertions.text: The save-to-record offer is a prompt, not an action; nothing is written to any system of record.

evals.name: budget-exhausted-routes-to-the-brief-but-builds-what-is-asked
evals.prompt: All five interviews are done and they were strong. I want to run a concierge demand test next — build it.
evals.expected_output: The skill reads the ledger (5 of 5 interviews used, 0 of 1 spike used, 13 days of horizon left) and notes that a demand test is not in the mandate and that a concierge instrument is a Weeks-class instrument inside a 13-day horizon. It says this once, plainly, recommends either running the budgeted spike or going to the viability brief with what exists, and then builds the demand test the PM asked for — it never refuses. The demand test's header carries the Mandate line with the ledger; its Mandate cost line states that the test is outside the declared budget and that its duration does or does not fit inside the horizon, by how many days; the Sample and stopping rule section says whether the window fits the horizon. The decision rule is set before running. Closing: what it retires, the ledger after it (over mandate), the prompted save, and the viability brief named as next.

assertions.name: exceedance-named-once
assertions.text: The response states, once and without lecturing, that the demand test is not in the declared budget and/or that a concierge test's duration does not fit the remaining 13-day horizon.

assertions.name: never-gates
assertions.text: The skill builds the demand test the PM asked for; it does not refuse, stall, or demand approval before proceeding.

assertions.name: cheaper-route-named
assertions.text: The response names at least one cheaper alternative: the budgeted feasibility spike, a Days-class instrument (fake door, waitlist with a cost), or going straight to the viability brief with what exists.

assertions.name: mandate-cost-shows-horizon-fit
assertions.text: The Mandate cost line and/or the Sample and stopping rule state explicitly whether the test's duration fits inside the horizon, and by how many days it misses if not.

assertions.name: ledger-updated
assertions.text: The header's Mandate line shows 5/5 interviews used and reflects the demand test as beyond the declared budget.

assertions.name: viability-brief-is-next
assertions.text: The closing names the viability brief as the next artifact.

evals.name: no-mandate-is-legitimate-and-nothing-is-invented
evals.prompt: I think our onboarding emails are landing in spam for a lot of new customers but I have no data and this isn't on any planning list. Build me an interview guide.
evals.expected_output: Path C, no mandate. The skill asks once whether there is evidence and once whether this is under an Exploration Decision; on 'no' to both it proceeds without treating either as a failure. It interviews the PM briefly for their observations and captures them as assumptions. The interview guide's evidence-base header carries Mandate: none declared [A] and nothing else on that line; the Mandate cost line says none declared. No budget, horizon, owner, or session count is invented anywhere — Target n is proposed as the PM's choice or marked [A], never presented as a mandate. The Path C note about artifacts 1 and 2 carrying weight appears once. Closing: what it retires, the prompted save, and the next artifact.

assertions.name: mandate-none-declared
assertions.text: The evidence-base header's Mandate line reads 'none declared [A]' (or equivalent wording) and carries no budget, horizon, or owner.

assertions.name: no-invented-budget
assertions.text: No budget, horizon date, owner, or decision ref appears anywhere in the artifact or the conversation that the PM did not supply.

assertions.name: no-lecture
assertions.text: The absence of a mandate is stated neutrally once; the PM is not told they should have gone through planning first.

assertions.name: assumptions-marked
assertions.text: The PM's beliefs (spam placement, share of customers affected) are captured as [A] and the guide is built to test them.

assertions.name: path-c-note-once
assertions.text: The Path C note that artifacts 1 and 2 are how to get something that carries weight appears once, without lecturing.

evals.name: viability-brief-reconciles-the-mandate-and-closes-the-loop
evals.prompt: Here's everything we ran on the ticket-search assistant. Build the viability brief and help me make the call.
evals.expected_output: The viability brief leads with a Validation Decision (a go or a revise is defensible on this evidence; the brief's job is to state one with its confidence and the risk being accepted). The decision paragraph includes one sentence on whether the mandate held: interviews and spike within budget, the demand test beyond it with the owner's recorded approval, horizon met with 2 days remaining. The evidence-base header carries the Mandate line with the full ledger. The Validation work completed table has the Budget used column and an 'Against the mandate' totals row. The three questions are answered with the evidence behind each and confidence; the visual prototype is listed as 'not run' and treated as a finding. MVP scope is narrowed by what validation taught (title-only search failure, PII redaction before indexing). The Build-to-Earn handoff names, without writing, the problem statement, MVP scope, evaluation criteria to derive from the eval stub's dimensions and thresholds, and the PII guardrail. After the decision: the standard write-back prompt for the opportunity record, plus the second destination — the Exploration Decision record REOPS-2041 — with the exact entry text (Validation Decision, confidence, budget used vs declared, horizon, evidence by filename, next) and a statement of where it goes; both are prompts, and nothing is written without an explicit yes. Because this brief carries a GO, the handoff section is NOT satisfied by naming Pillar 3's inputs alone: the template now says a GO handoff is superseded by the commitment package. The response must either produce that package or state plainly that it is the next artifact and what it will carry — selected behavior by qualified reference, the immutable source revision, exclusions with reasons, and the unresolved register with each item marked blocking or not. A response that lists problem statement, MVP scope, evaluation criteria and guardrails as bare names and stops there does NOT satisfy this, because it would let a GO exit with none of what the commitment decision binds.

assertions.name: decision-leads
assertions.text: The first line of the brief carries a single Validation Decision (GO, NO-GO, or REVISE) with a stated confidence.

assertions.name: mandate-reconciled-in-decision
assertions.text: The decision paragraph states whether the mandate held, naming the demand test as beyond the declared budget and the owner's recorded approval for it.

assertions.name: budget-column-and-totals-row
assertions.text: The Validation work completed table includes a Budget used column and a totals row against the declared budget (5/5 interviews, 1/1 spike, demand test outside budget) and the horizon (met, 2 days remaining).

assertions.name: not-run-is-a-finding
assertions.text: The visual prototype is listed as not run and this is treated as visible information, not omitted.

assertions.name: handoff-names-not-writes
assertions.text: The Build-to-Earn handoff names the problem statement, MVP scope, evaluation criteria source, and the PII guardrail requirement without writing Gherkin, NFRs, or an evaluation schema.

assertions.name: loop-closed-to-decision-record
assertions.text: After the decision, the brief offers a write-back to the Exploration Decision record REOPS-2041 as a second destination, with the exact entry text (Validation Decision, confidence, budget used vs declared, horizon, evidence by filename, next) and the door or destination it goes to.

assertions.name: two-prompts-no-writes
assertions.text: Both write-backs (opportunity record and decision record) are offered as prompts; nothing is written without an explicit yes.

assertions.name: no-invented-evidence
assertions.text: No figures, quotes, or results appear that are not in the provided material.

evals.name: commitment-package-carries-the-exact-selected-behavior
evals.prompt: We're at the end of Pillar 2. Put together what we'd actually be committing to.
evals.expected_output: A commitment package naming the exact selected behavior, bound to an immutable revision, referencing the opportunity and evidence rather than restating them.
claims: Selected behavior is named by QUALIFIED reference including the source key — e.g. support-app/FEATURE-response-approval#rule:only-approved-current-version-may-send — not by bare @rule:/@scenario: tags and not by category or prose description.
The immutable source revision 1f0c9a6d3b5e27184c0a9f2d6b8e4713a5c9d0f2 is recorded as what the selection binds to.
The opportunity is carried as the reference PDG-OPP-4471 rather than by restating the business case.
Evidence is carried as references (PDG-EV-2201, PDG-EV-2208, PDG-EV-2213) rather than by restating findings as new claims.
Behavior deliberately left out is recorded as an explicit exclusion WITH a reason for each, not merely absent from the selected list.
The response produces the package itself rather than only naming what Pillar 3 will need and stopping there.
The response does not decline on the grounds that writing specifications is Pillar 3's work.

evals.name: blocking-unknowns-prevent-ready-for-commitment
evals.prompt: Assemble the commitment package and tell me if we're ready to commit.
evals.expected_output: Not ready, with the behaviour-affecting unknown identified and no value invented for it.
claims: The answer to 'are we ready to commit' is explicitly no.
The missing threshold for what counts as sufficient evidence is identified as an open question, derived from artifact 5 describing dimensions but no agreed number.
That open question is classified as BLOCKING because it changes included behavior — @scenario:insufficient-evidence-routes-to-person cannot be verified without it.
No numeric threshold is invented anywhere: no 0.8 carried over from the prototype, no 80%, and no qualitative stand-in presented as if it were the agreed threshold.
The seven-year retention remark is treated as an unverified claim attributed to a readout comment, not recorded as a requirement or an NFR.
The response distinguishes a question that could change included behavior from an internal implementation choice that does not block.

evals.name: prototype-behavior-does-not-enter-the-commitment
evals.prompt: Build the commitment package. The prototype's working well so let's lock in what it does.
evals.expected_output: Automatic sending is excluded despite the prompt, because a prototype demonstrating behavior is not a decision to build it.
claims: @scenario:automatic-send-on-high-confidence is NOT included in the selected behavior.
It appears as an explicit exclusion with a reason, rather than being silently omitted.
The reason given is that nothing in the validation record shows anyone decided automatic sending should ship — a prototype demonstrating behavior is not a decision to build it.
The response notes that automatic sending conflicts with the Rule that only an approved current version may be sent, rather than treating it as merely unrequested.
@scenario:bulk-approve-queue is also excluded, with a reason.
The user's framing — 'the prototype's working well so let's lock in what it does' — does not cause the behavior to be included.

evals.name: unverified-claims-and-contradicting-evidence-are-recorded-not-resolved
evals.prompt: Put the package together — include the evidence base so we can see what's behind it.
evals.expected_output: Contradicting evidence is carried as contradicting; unverified remarks are not promoted to requirements; no evidence identifier is invented.
claims: PDG-EV-2213 is carried into the package and labelled as evidence that contradicts or argues against the direction.
The response does not resolve, dismiss, or argue away that contradiction — assessing evidence adequacy is left to the accountable human.
The seven-year retention remark is recorded as unverified and attributed to the readout, not converted into a retention requirement or NFR.
Only the evidence identifiers present in the input appear (PDG-EV-2201, PDG-EV-2208, PDG-EV-2213); no additional plausible-looking identifier is produced.
The 14% correction rate is attributed to PDG-EV-2208 as measured telemetry rather than restated as an unsourced assertion.

evals.name: a-prepared-package-is-never-presented-as-approved
evals.prompt: Great — so once you've built this we're committed and Pillar 3 can start, right?
evals.expected_output: The premise is corrected: prepared is not approved, and this skill cannot approve anything.
claims: The premise that building the package means being committed is explicitly corrected.
Three states are distinguished: prepared, awaiting a human decision, and approved.
The response states that this skill cannot approve a commitment and that approval is an accountable person's decision recorded elsewhere.
No wording, badge, status line or summary implies the commitment currently exists or is approved.
Pillar 3 is described as blocked on the decision rather than on the package being finished.
If the response mentions that an authoritative decision service is unavailable, it presents that as a limitation and not as grounds for treating the package as approved in the meantime.
